 THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed by the claimants under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988,
challenging the award dated 15.03.2018 in MVC No.5331/2017, passed by the III Additional Judge and MACT, Bengaluru (SCCH-18).
2.

The claimants filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the MV Act, seeking just and proper compensation on account of the death of their mother, Smt. Shashikala, wife of the late Chidananda,
who succumbed to injuries sustained in a road accident on 25.08.2017.
The Tribunal awarded a total compensation of Rs.13,74,000/- with interest at 9% per annum.
The claimants are now before this Court seeking an enhancement of the awarded compensation.

3. Having heard the learned counsel for the appellants/claimants and the learned counsel for the respondent- Insurance Company, it is noted that the death of Smt. Shashikala in the road traffic accident on 25.08.2017 is not disputed.
As of the date of the accident, the deceased was aged 34 years.

4. In the absence of proof of income, the notional income must be assessed as Rs.11,000/- according to the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for accidents occurring in the year 2017, as opposed to the Rs.7,000/- assessed by the Tribunal.

5. To this income, 40% should be added on account of future prospects, in line with the law established by the Supreme Court in 'NATIONAL INSURANCE CO. LTD. v. PRANAY SETHI AND Kum Shwetha C vs Icici Lombard General Insurance Co Ltd on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129279301/
2 OTHERS NC: 2024:KHC:22253 [AIR 2017 SC 5157]'.

sentences.text: Thus, the monthly income amounts to Rs.15,400/-.
Given that there are two dependents, it is appropriate to deduct one-third of the deceased's income towards personal expenses, leaving a remainder of Rs.10,267/- as her contribution to the family.
6. Considering that the deceased was 34 years old at the time of the accident, the applicable multiplier for her age group is '16'.
Therefore, the claimants are entitled to a compensation of Rs.19,71,264/- (Rs.10,267 * 12 * 16) on account of 'loss of dependency'.
Therefore, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is re- assessed as follows:
Sl . Heads

Amount  No. (In Rupees)
 1. Towards loss of Dependency 19,71,264  2. Towards loss of Estate 15,000  3. Towards Funeral Expenses 15,000  4.
Towards loss of Consortium 80,000
In the result, the appeal is allowed-in-part.
The judgment of the Claims Tribunal is modified.
The claimant is entitled for a total compensation of Rs.20,81,264/- as against Rs.13,74,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
8. The enhanced compensation amount of Rs.7,07,264/- shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing the petition till the date of realization.
To this extent, the impugned award stands modified.
